questions.statement: Juan ________ speak three languages: Spanish, English, and French.

options.feedback: Correct! "Can" expresses general ability in the present.
Incorrect. This is for past ability.
Incorrect. This is for permission or possibility.

questions.explanation:
El verbo modal "can" es la forma más común de expresar que alguien tiene la capacidad o habilidad de hacer algo en el presente.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: When I was five years old, I ________ ride a bike without help.

options.feedback: Correct! "Could" is the past form of "can" for general past abilities.

questions.explanation:
Para hablar de habilidades que teníamos en el pasado (que solíamos poseer), usamos "could".

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: ________ I use your dictionary for a moment, please?

options.feedback: Correct! "May" is a polite and formal way to ask for permission.
Incorrect. Too formal for this context.

questions.explanation:
Aunque "Can" se usa mucho informalmente, "May" es la forma correcta y más educada de pedir permiso en contextos escolares o formales.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: With enough practice, you ________ speak English fluently in a couple of years.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Can" doesn't have a future form.
Correct! We use "will be able to" for future abilities.

questions.explanation:
Como el modal "can" no tiene forma de futuro, debemos usar la estructura "will be able to" para hablar de capacidades futuras.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Take a jacket with you. It ________ get cold tonight.

options.feedback: Correct! "Might" expresses a possibility in the future.
Incorrect. "Can" is for general possibility, but for specific future events, "might" is better.

questions.explanation:
"Might" (y también "may") se utilizan para indicar que algo es posible en el futuro, aunque no estemos seguros de que ocurrirá.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: **Assistant:** "________ I help you find something, sir?"
questions.context: Asking for help in a shop.

options.feedback: Correct! Very common formal offer of help.

questions.explanation:
En el sector servicios, el uso de "May" o "Can" para ofrecer ayuda es la norma. "May" otorga un tono más profesional y servicial.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The fire was huge, but the firefighters ________ save everyone in the building.

options.feedback: Incorrect. "Could" is for general ability, not a specific success in one situation.
Correct! "Was/were able to" is preferred for a specific success in the past.

questions.explanation:
Para hablar de un logro específico en una situación difícil del pasado (no una habilidad general), preferimos "was/were able to" o "managed to" sobre "could".

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
**Speaker A:** "We may go to the park."
**Speaker B:** "We could go to the park."

Which speaker sounds like they are suggesting an **option** rather than just a possibility?

options.feedback: Correct! "Could" is often used to suggest options or choices.

questions.explanation:
Aunque ambos pueden indicar posibilidad, "could" tiene un uso pragmático muy común para proponer planes o alternativas.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: I can't find my wallet. I ________ have left it at the restaurant.

options.feedback: Correct! "Might have + participle" is used for past possibility/speculation.

questions.explanation:
Para especular sobre cosas que posiblemente ocurrieron en el pasado, usamos la estructura: modal (might/may/could) + have + participio pasado.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
Identify the error:
"I **haven't could (A)** finish the work yet, but I **hope (B)** I **will be able (C)** to do it **tomorrow (D)**."
questions.context: Identifying errors in modal usage across tenses.

options.feedback: Correct! Error found. "Can/could" cannot be used in the Present Perfect. It should be "haven't been able to".

questions.explanation:
Dado que los modales como "can" son "defectivos" (no tienen todas las formas), debemos usar "be able to" en tiempos compuestos como el Presente Perfecto.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which request is the most appropriate for a student asking a principal for help?

options.text: I want you to help me.
I wonder if you might be able to help me with this issue?
options.feedback: Correct! Very polite and uses "might be able to" to soften the request.

questions.explanation:
En niveles intermedios, se valora la capacidad de "suavizar" peticiones usando modales de posibilidad, lo que demuestra cortesía y respeto por la jerarquía.

---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement:
"In the past, people could only communicate across long distances by letters. Today, we can talk to anyone instantly via the internet. In the future, we might be able to communicate using only our thoughts."
What is the summary of this progression?
questions.context: Selecting the best conclusion about human ability.

options.text: Human communication abilities have evolved from slow methods to instant ones, with even more radical possibilities ahead.
options.feedback: Correct! It summarizes past (could), present (can) and future (might be able to).

options.text: People in the past were smarter because they could write letters.
The internet is the only way people can talk to each other now.
We must stop using technology to communicate.

questions.explanation: Sintetizar la evolución de una capacidad requiere el uso correcto de los diferentes modales que corresponden a cada marco temporal (pasado, presente y futuro).
